note: Rewritten from Light 1930, pp. 200—201; original in English; the original itself states that "Time and space permit but brief diagnoses, and measurements of the soldier and worker of the new species", so this entry has only diagnostic characters and measurements and no morphological description section; the value 1.03 in column B of the soldier postmentum constriction index is transcribed as printed. The description of the nest is in the same article, pp. 201—202.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alates not described. Soldier of the wheeleri species group, large, head width more than 1 mm; head nearly square, head constriction index about 0.95; head much lower relative to its height than in A. wheeleri; frons not steeply inclined, area smaller, hairs also fewer; mandibles inflected inward from the level of the tooth and then abruptly and strongly curved inward; notch deep but short and angular; inner face of the left basal projection straight; tooth not projecting, sharp, directed basally; postmentum almost without constriction. Worker large; abdomen long and slender in life (strongly contracted when preserved), contents dark, dirty grey to black; head round, yellow; antennae long, yellow; mandibles large, the first two teeth long and pointed, the first much longer than the second. The original author noted that the differences between this species and A. wheeleri are of specific rank, but that alates and more soldiers, if later collected, might show intergradation between the two.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: At the time of publication, limits of time and space allowed only diagnostic characters and the measurements of the soldier and worker; no complete morphological description was given. Soldier measurements (mm; three soldiers, A, B, C): head length 1.36 (A), 1.35 (B), 1.32 (C); head width 1.02 (A), 1.04 (B); minimum head width 0.96 (A), 0.96 (B); mandible length 0.86 (A), 0.90 (B), 0.86 (C); postmentum length 0.68 (A), 0.66 (B); maximum postmentum width 0.35 (A), 0.33 (B); minimum postmentum width 0.34 (A), 0.34 (B), 0.34 (C); pronotum width 0.66 (A), 0.66 (B); head index 0.75 (A), 0.77 (B); head constriction index 0.94 (A), 0.92 (B); head-mandible index 0.63 (A), 0.67 (B), 0.65 (C); postmentum constriction index 0.94 (A), 1.03 (B), 1.00 (C).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Worker measurements (mm; three workers, A, B, C): head length 0.83 (A), 0.84 (C); head width 1.00 (C); pronotum width 0.60 (A), 0.68 (B), 0.68 (C).

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Nest: the nest body consists mainly of dense, dark brownish-black material that looks like soil but is mostly, if not entirely, carton. The nest is 24 in. high, about 24 in. in circumference at ground level, somewhat pear-shaped, about 6 in. of it exposed above ground and the rest buried in compacted sand; many galleries lined with characteristic dark carton extend from the nest in all directions. The base of the nest surrounds the root of a dead plant and is abandoned; the great majority of the termites are in the upper half of the nest. It nests in sand, often attacks wood buried in sand, and builds sand galleries lined with carton.
